## Epistemic State

### Historical Fact

The Phase II cooperative agreement was awarded to Lockheed Martin on 2 July 1996. The composite liquid
hydrogen tank failed on 3 November 1999 at Marshall Space Flight Center, after its test programme had been
completed successfully and the tank drained, with the separation occurring approximately fifteen minutes
later. The investigation ran from mid-November 1999 to early February 2000 and reported a combination of
causes including microcracking with hydrogen infiltration, cryopumping of the nitrogen purge, elevated core
pressures, reduced bondline strength and toughness, and manufacturing flaws. The liquid oxygen tank was
aluminium, chosen under a contractual option for schedule reasons. The flight speed objective was reduced
from Mach 15 to Mach 13.8 during detailed design because projected weight exceeded requirements. The
programme was cancelled in the early months of 2001 without a flight. The Government Accountability Office
reported the agency contribution to the agreement at 912.4 million dollars and the industry contribution at
an estimated 286.6 million as of 1999.

### Engineering Analysis

The propellant mass fraction of 0.8898 required for orbit, and the 86.4 to 90.3 percent bracket across the
sensitivity sweep, are this article's derivation from the rocket equation under stated assumptions about
velocity requirement and specific impulse. The hydrogen volume share of 74.5 percent, the bulk density
figures and the ratio of 2.982 are arithmetic on published densities and the engine mixture ratio. The
membrane vessel mass law with shape factors of three halves and two is standard and is re-derived here. The
ideal tank fractions of 2.852 and 0.343 percent depend on assumed material allowables and are swept. The web
tension result, that it equals pressure times centre separation, is derived here and its limiting cases
check.
**The identity that the membrane mass per unit enclosed volume of a lobed section equals that of a cylinder exactly is derived here, verified to machine precision on the X-33 geometry, verified against numerically obtained area and arc length rather than closed forms, and tested as a randomised property over twenty thousand admissible geometries.**
The cryopumping fill fractions and the constant-volume warming pressure are ideal gas arithmetic. The
thermal mismatch strain of 1.306 percent and its ratio of 2.18 to the transverse failure strain rest on
assumed ply properties which are typical rather than measured. The nozzle comparison is ideal
one-dimensional flow and is checked against the sonic condition. The weight growth inversion of 9.9 to 12.6
percent is derived from the published speed objectives and is checked forward.

### Inference

**That the failure mechanism was thermodynamically forced rather than a workmanship defect is an inference, and it rests on the thermal mismatch arithmetic alone.**
The position of manufacturing flaws within the investigation's list of five causes is not evidence either
way,
**because the published summaries order those five differently and a list of contributing causes is not a ranking.**
The arithmetic is the whole of the support. It is a strong inference and it is not a finding of the
investigation.

**That the cancellation was decided by mass rather than by the tank failure is an inference**, and the
Government Accountability Office's programme-management reading is a competing account that the record
supports at least as well.

**That the linear scale ratio of 1.972 corroborates the half-scale description** is an inference from two
published masses under a cube law, and a vehicle is not a geometrically similar object.

### What the Record Does Not Settle

**Whether VentureStar's tanks could have reached the required efficiency is not settled by anything here.**
This article shows that a factor between 1.6 and 4.1 was needed depending on the budget allowed, and that no
such factor had been demonstrated. It does not show that the factor was unreachable.

**Whether the programme would have been cancelled without the tank failure is not settled**, and the
counterfactual is unanswerable in principle.

**The reported relative weights of the composite and aluminium-lithium tanks are not settled** by any
primary source this article could retrieve.

**The precise cancellation date is given variously as February and as March 2001** in the sources consulted,
and the article says early 2001 rather than choosing.

## Out of Scope

The base-flow and plume behaviour of a truncated plug nozzle, which is the genuinely difficult part of the
aerospike architecture. The detailed aerothermodynamics of the lifting-body shape. The guidance and control
design in any depth. The X-34, which was cancelled alongside the X-33 and which this series treats
separately. The Space Launch Initiative that followed. The commercial and financial case for VentureStar,
including the market forecasts that underwrote it. The politics of the cancellation decision.

## Conclusion

**The X-33 was cancelled because its demonstration worked.**

That is not a paradox and it is not a defence of the programme. A technology demonstrator exists to find out
whether a technology will do what a vehicle needs.
**The X-33's tank was built, was tested, and returned an answer**, and the answer was legible in two
independent ways. It failed in a manner that showed the linerless composite sandwich cryotank of that
generation was not ready, and, separately and more damningly,
**it weighed 26.83 percent of the hydrogen it held, which extrapolates to 41.0 percent of VentureStar's entire structural allowance.**
The second number needed no failure to be true.

**The chain that produced the failure is the article's main technical contribution and it runs one way.**
Land on a runway, and the vehicle is a lifting body. Make it a lifting body, and the tank must be conformal.
Make it conformal, and it must be lobed. Lobe it, and the walls carry bending. Carry bending, and the wall
is a sandwich. Build a sandwich, and there is a core, and the core is a sealed void against liquid hydrogen
at twenty kelvin. **Every link is forced by the one before it.**

**And the membrane model, which is the model a designer reaches for, says the whole chain is free.** The
identity derived here is exact. The web costs precisely what the volume it encloses is worth, at every
radius and every separation.
**A cost model that returns zero for a decision that turned out to be expensive is not a small problem, and locating the missing terms, namely bending, buckling, minimum gauge and joints, is the practical lesson.**

**Set beside the previous article the pair is instructive.** The [X-32][related_post_a329_boeing_x32] was
flown against a rival and could not answer its question, because neither demonstrator was the aircraft being
bought. The X-33 never flew and could answer its question, because the quantity that mattered was
scale-invariant and could be weighed on the ground.
**A vehicle that never left the ground produced a cleaner result than one that flew one hundred and forty-four times**,
which is a statement about experimental design rather than about either aeroplane.

**The designation went to a vehicle that was never finished, and the programme still found something out.**
This series has now met a designation marking an absence of demand in the
[X-27][related_post_a324_lockheed_x27], an absence of knowledge in the
[X-30][related_post_a327_rockwell_x30], and, here, **the presence of an answer nobody wanted.**
